To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose two mathematical formulations to provision and route network slices on the underlying physical network, we propose an algorithm to reconfigure the network slices in a dynamic fashion, we validate the proposed models with realistic traffic data from a real city, and we compare the results with a baseline solution.

the models are capable of provisioning network slices in a dynamic way to satisfy the traffic demand and the QoS requirements, while minimizing the interruption of service, energy consumption and the probability of blocking traffic.

we propose two mathematical programming models for the dynamic provisioning of network slices on the underlying physical network, with the goal of minimizing a linear combination between the probability of blocking traffic demands, the energy consumption of network devices and the interruption of service due the reconfiguration of slices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How to provision network slices on a physical network?
the dynamic reconfiguration of network slices in the physical network in order to optimize the resource consumption and the service interruption.

the development of a dynamic provisioning model for network slices in Software Defined Optical Networks, which is able to optimize the network resource usage, the traffic delivery, and the network reconfiguration, in a cost-effective manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this thesis has been able to propose two mathematical models for the dynamic provisioning of network slices on the underlying physical network, with the aim to minimize a combination of probability of traffic requests blocking, energy consumption of network devices and interruption due to the reconfigurations of network slices.
the proposed mathematical models are able to provide an efficient and effective dynamic provisioning of network slices in a software defined metro core network.

the proposed models are able to dynamically provision slices in a physical network, complying their QoS requirements, while minimizing the probability of blocking, energy consumption of network resources and interruption of service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed models allow to dynamically provision network slicing in software defined metro optical networks, optimizing the resource usage of the underlying infrastructure and minimizing the probability of blocking traffic demands, the energy consumption and the interruption of service.

, by means of the proposed models and algorithms, we are able to dynamically reconfigure the network slices to provide a better service to users, while optimizing the resources of the underlying physical network.

we propose a novel approach to dynamically provision network services in optical networks, which is able to predict the traffic evolution and to reconfigure network slices accordingly to the predicted traffic evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model is able to dynamically adapt network slices to the traffic demand, reducing energy consumption and avoiding blocking requests.
the dynamic reconfiguration of network slices is a key factor for the optimization of resource allocation, especially in the case of a high traffic variability.
the proposed models can effectively optimize the network slice allocation, while considering QoS constraints and energy consumption.
